examples.ko: 아이가 열이 나서 어린이집에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: The child had a fever, so they couldn't go to daycare.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 체온계로 열을 재 보세요.
examples.en: Take your temperature with a thermometer before you go to bed.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸리면 열도 나고 기침도 해요.
examples.en: When you catch a cold, you get a fever and also cough.

examples.ko: 열 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep at night because of the fever.

examples.ko: 열만 내리면 내일 학교에 가도 돼요.
examples.en: Once the fever goes down, you can go to school tomorrow.

explain: '열이 나다/오르다 ↔ 열이 내리다'처럼 써요. 숫자 10을 뜻하는 '열'과 소리가 같으니 앞뒤 말로 구별해요. 체온을 잴 때는 '열을 재다'라고도 하고 '체온을 재다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 친구가 약속에 또 늦어서 너무 열 받았어요.
phrases.en: My friend was late again, and I got really worked up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 많이 난다는 편한 말투예요. 친구처럼 가까운 사이에서 쓰고, 어른께 말할 때는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you are very angry. Use it with friends, not with elders or in formal situations.

explain_en: It is used as in '열이 나다/오르다' and the opposite '열이 내리다'. It sounds the same as '열' (ten), so use the surrounding words to tell them apart. For taking your temperature, people say both '열을 재다' and '체온을 재다'.

t90.ax: Today I have no fever, I only cough.

examples.en: The rent went up too much, so I'm planning to move.

explain: 집 전체보다 방 하나를 빌릴 때 느낌이 강해요. 집 전체에 대한 월 임대료는 '월세'나 '집세'라고 해요. '방세를 내다', '방세가 밀리다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I pay the rent at the end of every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방세와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 방세.

phrases.en: The rent is overdue because I didn't have money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제때 내지 못해 쌓였다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the rent has piled up unpaid.

phrases.en: The monthly rent for this house is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '방세'와 비슷하지만 집 전체에 대해서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 방세 but also used for a whole house.

explain_en: It feels more like renting a single room than a whole home. For monthly rent on a whole place, people say '월세' or '집세'. Common patterns are '방세를 내다' and '방세가 밀리다'.

t90.ax: I'm very worried about the rent.

examples.ko: 병원에서 낸 수술비가 생각보다 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The surgery cost I paid at the hospital was more than I expected.

examples.ko: 수술비는 보험으로 일부 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get part of the surgery cost back through insurance.
I cashed in my savings account to raise the money for my parents' surgery.
I asked the hospital how much the surgery would cost.

examples.ko: 아버지 수술비 때문에 걱정이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: I'm really worried because of my father's surgery costs.
You have to pay the surgery fee before being discharged.

explain: '수술비가 들다·나오다', '수술비를 내다·마련하다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. 병원에서 쓰는 돈 전체는 '병원비'라고 하고, '치료비'는 치료에 드는 돈이에요. 같은 방식으로 '입원비', '검사비'도 있어요.

phrases.en: I paid for my father's surgery costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for paying money.

phrases.en: This operation cost a lot in surgery fees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용이 필요하다는 뜻으로, 얼마나 드는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the cost is required; used to say how much it takes.

phrases.en: I'm saving money to come up with the surgery cost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 돈을 미리 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to prepare the needed money in advance.

explain_en: It pairs with fixed verbs: '수술비가 들다/나오다' (the cost comes to) and '수술비를 내다/마련하다' (pay/raise the cost). '병원비' covers hospital money overall, while '치료비' is the cost of treatment. In the same pattern there are '입원비' (hospitalization) and '검사비' (testing).

examples.ko: 대학교 입학금을 내야 해서 아르바이트를 해요.
examples.en: I have to pay the university admission fee, so I work part-time.
The admission fee and tuition are paid separately.
I called the academy to ask how much the admission fee is.

examples.ko: 어학당에 등록하면 입학금은 한 번만 내요.
examples.en: If you register at the language school, you pay the admission fee only once.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 입학금을 면제해 주는 행사가 있대요.
examples.en: I heard there's an event this month that waives the admission fee.

explain: 입학할 때 처음 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 학기마다 내는 돈은 '등록금', 학원에서 매달 내는 돈은 '수강료'라고 구분해요. '입학금을 내다/면제하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I have to pay the admission fee by next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불하는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for paying the fee.

phrases.en: Tuition is paid every semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입학금과 달리 학기마다 내는 돈이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the admission fee, it is paid every semester.

phrases.en: That academy's admission fee is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금액이 많고 적음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the amount is high or low.

explain_en: One-time fee paid when entering a school (새 학교에 내야 하는 입학금을 오늘 은행에서 냈어요.) It's money paid once when you first enter a school. Money paid each semester is '등록금', and monthly fees at an academy are '수강료'. Use it as '입학금을 내다' (pay) or '면제하다' (waive).

t90.ax: The admission fee and tuition are paid separately.

en: to be provided; to be offered

examples.en: Breakfast is provided free at the hotel.
The class materials will be provided by email.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 학생에게만 제공돼서 학생증이 필요해요.
examples.en: This service is only offered to students, so you need a student ID.
I'm looking for a cafe that offers Wi-Fi.
Lunch is provided and travel costs are covered too.

explain: '제공하다'는 주는 쪽, '제공되다'는 받는 쪽에서 본 말이에요. 안내문에서 '무료 제공', '제공됩니다'를 자주 봐요. '주다'보다 격식 있어서 가게, 회사, 서비스 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Water and coffee are provided for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 호텔에서 돈을 받지 않고 준다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for things a shop or hotel gives at no charge.

phrases.en: A translation service is offered in this app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 회사가 어떤 서비스를 준비해 두었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an app or company has a service available.

phrases.example: 이 방에는 아침 식사가 제공되지 않아요.
phrases.en: Breakfast is not provided in this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 안내문이나 설명에서 '없다'는 뜻을 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form politely says something is not offered.

explain_en: Service or item is offered, no receiver stated (무료로 제공되다) 제공하다 is seen from the giver's side and 제공되다 from the receiving side. You often see 무료 제공 or 제공됩니다 in notices. It is more formal than 주다, so it fits shops, companies, and services.

t90.ax: Breakfast is provided free at the hotel.

examples.en: This shop sells Korean snacks.

examples.ko: 그 빵집은 아침 일곱 시부터 빵을 판매했어요.
examples.en: That bakery sold bread from seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 이 식당에서는 점심에 도시락을 판매하지 않아요.
examples.en: This restaurant doesn't sell boxed lunches at lunchtime.
If you sell goods, you have to pay taxes.

explain: 가게나 회사가 물건을 파는 일이라서 안내문, 광고, 뉴스에 잘 나와요. 일상에서는 '팔다'가 더 자연스러워서 '이거 팔아요?'라고 물어요. 반대말은 '구매하다'와 '사다'예요. 개인이 중고 물건을 파는 건 '중고로 팔았어요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Do you sell this?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '판매하다'보다 '팔다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 팔다 is more natural than 판매하다.

phrases.en: This book is on sale at bookstores.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 팔고 있다는 뜻으로 안내문이나 광고에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is being sold now, common in notices and ads.

phrases.en: This shop does not sell cigarettes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게가 팔지 않는 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what a shop does not sell.

explain_en: You sell goods as business; formal, shops. It is used when shops or companies sell goods, so you see it in notices, ads, and news. In daily talk '팔다' is more natural: '이거 팔아요?' The opposites are '구매하다' and '사다'. A private person selling a used item says '중고로 팔았어요'.

dis.h: sell goods; formal, shops and business
gh: sell off a building, company, or assets
launch a product on the market

p.n: Same meaning; 팔다 is plainer and more conversational.

examples.en: Our youngest son got into university this time.
The youngest son still acts spoiled.
Grandmother cherishes her youngest son the most.

examples.ko: 동네 어르신이 저를 보고 '자네, 이 집 막내아들 아닌가?' 하고 물으셨어요.
examples.en: A neighborhood elder looked at me and asked, 'Aren't you the youngest son of this house?'
The whole family gathered for the youngest son's wedding.

explain: '막내'만 말해도 되지만 아들임을 밝히고 싶을 때 '막내아들'이라고 해요. 짝말은 '맏아들'이고, 딸이면 '막내딸'이에요. 집안에서 막내는 귀여움을 받는 자리라 '막내아들은 아직도 어리광을 부려요' 같은 말이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I am the youngest in my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아들인지 딸인지 말하지 않고 가장 어린 자녀를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the youngest child without saying son or daughter.

phrases.en: I was born the youngest son of three brothers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'를 붙여 어떤 자리로 태어났는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -(으)로 says what position in the family you were born into.
phrases.en_equiv: to be born the youngest son

phrases.en: The eldest son works at a company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 먼저 태어난 아들을 말하고, 막내아들과 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first-born son, the opposite of 막내아들.

explain_en: '막내' alone is enough, but you say '막내아들' when you want to make clear it is a son. Its counterpart is '맏아들' (eldest son), and for a daughter it is '막내딸'. The youngest is often the one who gets doted on at home, so a sentence like '막내아들은 아직도 어리광을 부려요' sounds natural.

examples.en: It's hard to bear hunger during class.

examples.ko: 저는 배고픔 때문에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of hunger.
If I skip breakfast, the hunger gets bad.

examples.ko: 배고픔보다 졸음이 더 힘들 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes sleepiness is harder to bear than hunger.

explain: 말할 때는 '배고픔'보다 '배고프다', '배가 고프다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '배고픔'은 글이나 설명에서 그 상태를 하나의 말로 부를 때 어울려요. '배고픔을 참다', '배고픔을 느끼다'처럼 정해진 동사와 같이 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 아침을 안 먹어서 배가 너무 고파요.
phrases.en: I didn't eat breakfast, so I'm very hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '배고픔'보다 이 표현이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, this is much more natural than 배고픔.

phrases.en: I endured my hunger and exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배고픔'과 함께 외우면 좋은 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good collocation to memorize with 배고픔.

phrases.en: I suddenly felt hungry at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 상태를 설명하는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits writing or slightly formal speech that describes the state.

explain_en: In speech people say '배고프다' or '배가 고프다' far more than 배고픔. 배고픔 fits writing or explanations, when you name the state as a noun. It is useful to memorize it with its usual verbs, as in '배고픔을 참다' and '배고픔을 느끼다'.

t90.ax: I can't sleep because of hunger.

en: to be taken ill; to catch a disease

examples.ko: 그 일로 병난 사람이 한둘이 아니에요.

explain: '병이 나다'를 붙여 쓴 말이에요. 그냥 '아프다'보다 무리하거나 걱정해서 몸이 상했다는 느낌이 강해요. '몸살이 나다', '탈이 나다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: If you overdo it, you'll get sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병나다'를 띄어 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 병나다.

phrases.en: I stayed up all night yesterday and got body aches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피곤해서 온몸이 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you ache all over from exhaustion.
phrases.en_equiv: to come down with body aches

phrases.en: I'm worried I might get sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아플까 걱정하는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express worry about getting sick.

explain_en: It is '병이 나다' written as one word. Compared with plain '아프다', it more strongly suggests that overwork or worry has worn the body down. It is used much like '몸살이 나다' or '탈이 나다'.

examples.ko: 이 영상은 하루 만에 수십만 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of thousands of people watched this video in one day.
I heard hundreds of thousands gathered at that singer's concert.

examples.ko: 수십만 개가 팔렸는데도 재고가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Even though hundreds of thousands were sold, there is still stock left.

examples.ko: 한 달 월세가 수십만 원이라 부담돼요.
examples.en: The monthly rent is hundreds of thousands of won, so it's a burden.
Roughly several hundred thousand people live in this city.

explain: 정확한 숫자를 모르거나 어림해서 말할 때 '수십만 명', '수십만 원'처럼 단위와 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '수만', '수백만'이 있고, 말할 때는 '몇십만'이라고도 해요. 보통 뒤에 오는 단위와 띄어 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 공연에 수십만 명이 모였어요.
phrases.en: Hundreds of thousands of people gathered for that singer's concert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수를 어림해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to roughly state a number of people.

phrases.en: The trip cost hundreds of thousands of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈의 액수를 어림해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to roughly state an amount of money.

phrases.en: Hundreds of thousands of people watched that video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '수십만' 대신 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken alternative to 'susimman'.

explain_en: Use it with a counter like '수십만 명' or '수십만 원' when you don't know or are estimating the exact number. Similar words are '수만' (tens of thousands) and '수백만' (millions), and in speech people also say '몇십만'. It is normally written with a space before the counter.

examples.en: Lower-grade kids finish class early.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 아직 저학년이라 숙제가 적어요.
examples.en: My child is still in the lower grades, so there's little homework.

examples.ko: 저학년 때는 친구랑 노는 게 제일 중요해요.
examples.en: In the lower grades, playing with friends matters most.

examples.ko: 이 책은 초등학교 저학년이 읽기에 좋아요.
examples.en: This book is good for lower-grade elementary students to read.

examples.ko: 저는 저학년 동생들을 가르치는 봉사를 해요.
examples.en: I volunteer teaching younger lower-grade kids.

examples.ko: 저학년에게는 긴 설명보다 그림이 더 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For lower-grade students, pictures help more than long explanations.

explain: 반대말은 '고학년'이에요. 보통 초등학교에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 학교에 따라 어느 학년까지인지는 조금 달라요. '저학년용', '저학년 때'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I was short in the lower grades.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어릴 적 학교 시절을 돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when looking back on early school years.

phrases.en: This book is for lower grades, so it's easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저학년 학생에게 맞게 만든 물건에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it to things made for lower-grade students.

phrases.en: Lower grades and upper grades have different lunch times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '고학년'과 짝으로 써서 학년을 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite '고학년' to divide students by grade.

explain_en: The opposite is '고학년' (upper grades). It's mostly used for elementary school, and exactly which grades count varies a bit by school. It often takes endings like '저학년용' (for lower grades) or '저학년 때' (when in the lower grades).

examples.en: My shoulders hurt, so I got a massage.
Sitting in a massage chair relieves my tiredness.
The massage felt so good that I got sleepy.
This hotel also has a massage service.
I showed my thanks to my grandmother with a massage.
Drink plenty of water after a massage.

explain: '안마 의자', '안마기'처럼 쓰는 말이고, 가게에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 같이 써요. 가족의 어깨를 풀어 드릴 때는 '주물러 드리다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I sat in the massage chair and rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 풀어 주는 의자를 말하고, 집이나 가게에서 많이 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: A chair that massages the body, common at home and in shops.

phrases.en: I got a foot massage yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서는 '안마'보다 '마사지'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: At shops, people say 마사지 more often than 안마.

phrases.en: I loosen my shoulders with a massager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 대고 쓰는 작은 기계를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a small device used on the body.

explain_en: Traditional pressing massage for sore muscles and stiffness. It appears in words like 안마 의자 and 안마기, and shops also use the word 마사지. When you rub a family member's shoulders, you can also say 주물러 드리다.

t90.ax: My shoulders hurt, so I got a massage.

examples.en: My child loves jelly so much.
Jelly is soft and very sweet.
I bought a fruit jelly at the convenience store.

examples.ko: 젤리를 많이 먹으면 이가 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat a lot of jelly, your teeth may hurt.
I brought jelly when I went to the movie theater.
I gave my friend some bear-shaped jelly.

explain: 한국에서 '젤리'는 과일즙으로 굳힌 디저트보다 말랑하고 쫀득한 과자를 먼저 떠올리는 경우가 많아요. 편의점에는 곰 모양, 과일 모양 젤리가 많아요. 우유와 달걀로 만든 부드러운 '푸딩'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: I bought a bag of jelly at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젤리는 봉지에 담아서 팔아서 '한 봉지'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Jelly candy is sold in bags, so it is counted as 한 봉지.

phrases.example: 동생은 곰 모양 젤리를 제일 좋아해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling likes the bear-shaped jelly the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모양'을 붙여 젤리가 어떤 모양인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 모양 describes the shape of the jelly.

phrases.en: This shop has tasty fruit jelly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛이나 재료를 앞에 붙여 젤리 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the flavor or ingredient in front to name the kind of jelly.

explain_en: In Korea, '젤리' often brings to mind a soft, chewy candy first rather than a fruit-juice dessert. Convenience stores sell many bear-shaped and fruit-shaped jellies. It differs from '푸딩', a soft dessert made with milk and eggs.

examples.en: I'm talking on the phone with my friend at the office now.
I talked with my mother on the phone for an hour yesterday.
I'd like to talk on the phone for a moment; is now okay?
I'm on a call right now, so I'll phone you later.
I'm too busy today, so it's hard to talk on the phone.

examples.ko: 회의 때문에 오래 통화할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't talk on the phone for long because of the meeting.

explain: '전화하다'는 전화를 거는 행동이고, '통화하다'는 연결돼서 서로 말하는 데 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '통화 중이에요', '통화가 안 돼요'처럼 연결 상태를 말할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 '친구와 통화하다'처럼 '와/과'랑 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I'm on the phone with my mother now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 전화로 말하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you are talking on the phone right now.

phrases.en: I can't get through to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전화가 연결되지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a phone call won't connect.

phrases.en: I talked on the phone with a friend for a long time yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 전화로 이야기한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for a phone talk that already happened.

explain_en: '전화하다' is the act of making a call, while '통화하다' focuses on being connected and actually talking. That is why you also hear '통화 중이에요' (the line is busy) and '통화가 안 돼요' (I can't get through). It usually goes with '와/과', as in '친구와 통화하다'.

examples.en: I often listen to pop music.
I heard a pop singer is coming to Korea.
This song mixes pop and K-pop.
Many of my friends study English through pop songs.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 팝을 들으면서 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I danced while listening to pop.
Do you like music other than pop too?

explain: '팝'은 혼자보다 '팝 음악', '팝 가수'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙을 때가 많아요. '팝송'은 보통 영어 노래를 가리키고, 한국 노래는 '가요'나 'K팝'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I study English with pop songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보통 영어로 된 외국 노래를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually refers to foreign songs, mostly in English.

phrases.example: 그 팝 스타는 노래도 춤도 잘해요.
phrases.en: That pop star is good at both singing and dancing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기 많은 팝 가수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a popular pop singer.

phrases.en: I'm going to a pop concert this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팝' 뒤에 행사 이름을 붙여서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 팝 is often followed by an event word like this.

explain_en: 팝 usually appears with another word, as in 팝 음악 and 팝 가수. 팝송 normally means English-language songs, while Korean songs are called 가요 or K팝.
